title: Splitting a large factor does not decrease the product
summary: Larger integer factors can be split further without decreasing the product.
context: In maximum product cutting, test whether an integer factor n should be split further by comparing n against the product of 2 and n - 2.
description: Above sits a gray bar of length n; below sits an equal-length bar split at a vertical dashed line into a short green "2" on the left and a blue "n - 2" on the right, captioned below "When n ≥ 4, 2(n - 2) ≥ n always holds. Thus the final partition should contain only factors 1, 2, 3".

frames.title: Splitting a large factor does not decrease the product
frames.explanation: Because 2(n - 2) - n = n - 4, the product stays equal at n = 4 and strictly increases for n > 4. Repeatedly splitting factors of 4 or greater never decreases the product. Thus at least one optimal split uses only 1, 2, and 3. An optimal split may also retain a 4.
